picks.title: Introducing AlphaProof Code: a breakthrough in verifying complex software at depth
picks.rationale: This is DeepMind's own announcement of a new system in which LLM agents write Lean proofs. It machine-verified the compiled code of Signal's cryptographic protocol in about four weeks.
picks.excerpt: DeepMind's AlphaProof Code uses multiple LLM agents to write Lean proofs for software verification; it machine-verified the compiled code of Signal's cryptographic protocol in about four weeks, generating over six million lines of Lean and flagging ~1% of the codebase for human review.

picks.title: Google Researchers Use AI And Mathematical Proofs to Cut Quantum Computing Requirements
picks.rationale: A new paper (arXiv 2611.09822) in which agent teams with Lean-checked proofs cut quantum program costs 2.5x to 11x on chemistry and fusion workloads. It reports a result, not the earlier competition announcement.
picks.excerpt: Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI used teams of AI agents with Lean-checked proofs to design quantum programs, cutting combined qubit-and-gate costs about 11x for a fusion simulation, 8x for photochemistry and 2.5x for a drug-metabolism model (arXiv 2611.09822).

picks.title: Researcher uses AI to predict probabilities for chemical processes
picks.rationale: A peer-reviewed case in which AI agents wrote most of an open-source quantum chemistry code (vibe-qc). Cross-checking against an independent code caught its errors, which gives researchers a concrete verification practice.
picks.excerpt: University of Bonn chemist Michael Peintinger had AI agents write most of vibe-qc, an open-source quantum chemistry program for molecules and crystals, under his supervision; cross-checks against an independent code caught errors and confirmed results (Journal of Computational Chemistry).

picks.title: AI, computer graphics and wave optics combine for more realistic holographic VR/AR displays
picks.rationale: HKU trained a learned optics model on camera measurements and paired it with mesh-based hologram generation for sharper holographic VR/AR. This is new optics research published in Nature Communications and ACM TOG.
picks.excerpt: University of Hong Kong researchers trained a learned optics model on camera measurements to correct imperfections in a holographic display, and paired it with mesh-based hologram generation for smoother focus and sharper detail in lab prototypes (Nature Communications, ACM TOG).

picks.title: Prior expertise may determine whether AI builds skills or substitutes for them, field experiment suggests
picks.rationale: A three-month randomized field trial (Autor and Google, NBER) with 133 patent lawyers. AI raised junior lawyers' drafts most, but on a later no-AI task only the senior lawyers who had used it kept the skill gain.
picks.excerpt: A three-month randomized trial with 133 U.S. patent lawyers (MIT's David Autor and Google, NBER working paper) found an AI writing assistant improved drafts most for juniors, but on a later no-AI task only senior lawyers who had used the tool outperformed peers.

dedup.note: Dropped as duplicates: (1) QuEra/Harvard/Anthropic 'Use AI to Reduce Quantum Circuit Resource Requirements' (TQI 11-10). It is the same Claude-designs-leaner-quantum-circuits research published 10-18 (thequantuminsider.com/2026/10/17/anthropics-claude-designs-leaner-quantum-circuits...), its arXiv 2610.22367 is an October paper, and it reports no new release. (2) GEN 'New AI Models Are Turbo-Charging Protein Design' is an analysis feature on the running protein-design story (10-24 Nvidia/IPD, 11-04 text-to-protein) with no new event. It was also dropped on 11-10. Not picked on merit: the human-involvement creative-writing study (PNAS Nexus, close in theme to the 10-29 'AI may quickly generate ideas, but working with people leads to more creative ones'), the battery cathode GAN (EurekAlert, 11-03, related to the 10-22 sodium-ion story), the uranium-enrichment ML study, fish schooling ML, MLP Copilot aluminum oxidation, and Universe Today buried rocks. The Google quantum paper is a research result, distinct from the 10-24 $150k competition launch, and distinct from AlphaProof Code (software verification), even though both are Google and Lean-based. Diversity: 5 distinct outlets. Cross-section check: none of the picks touch any cross-section assignment in the curator brief (Adobe MAX, UE 5.9, Framestore/Sky, Businesses in ChatGPT, Gemini healthcare, Pixel Drop), and none involve biosecurity topics. published_urls.json (4242 lines) was too large to read in full without grep, so the all-section exact-URL grep was NOT completed. The orchestrator should run it before roll.
